results.title: If This Volcano Goes, Everyone On Earth Will Feel It — And The Signs Are Stacking Up
results.description:
If a volcano woke up near you, could its ash reach your house? Learn to read alert levels and ash reports, and check your own address: https://breakpointstore.net

Anak Krakatau, the volcano growing out of the caldera Krakatoa left behind in 1883, went back to Level III on Friday after 14 eruptions in four days, and within hours a magnitude 7.7 earthquake tore through Panama almost exactly on the opposite side of the planet. A theory spreading online says the pairing repeats 1882, when a great Panama quake struck less than a year before the eruption that cooled the whole world. The 700-kilometer antipode, the new moon timing and the 1882 date are all real. What none of them answers is which event came first on Friday, and what the volcano's own instruments say comes next.

Breakpoint covers the moments when the Earth shifts — earthquakes, eruptions, severe weather, climate events, and the science behind the planet's biggest stories. Every video delivers the headlines, the data, and what comes next in twenty to twenty-five minutes.

New videos three to four times a week.

results.title: THE KRAKATOA TRAGEDY: The Island That Exploded, but the Sea Was Worse | Full Documentary
results.description:
On Monday, 27 August 1883, the volcanic island of Krakatoa, in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, exploded with what may have been the loudest sound the Earth has ever made. But for the towns on the coasts around it, the worst came from the sea.

At about six o'clock that morning, on the beach at Anjer, a port on the western tip of Java, an old Dutch harbour pilot was walking along the shore under a sky black with ash when he saw a dark shape travelling toward him through the gloom. It was a ridge of water many metres high. The volcano had been exploding without a pause for sixteen hours, and nobody on those coasts had imagined that the danger would come from the water.

At two minutes past ten, Krakatoa exploded for the third time. Most of the island collapsed into the sea, and the sound was heard nearly five thousand kilometres away, on the island of Rodrigues in the Indian Ocean. The waves that followed rose up to thirty and forty metres on the coasts of the strait. At Merak, only two or three of some 2,700 people survived. In the bay of Telok Betong, the steamer Loudon saved itself by turning straight into the wave, while the gunboat Berouw was carried inland and left among the palm trees.

The official count of the dead was 36,417, almost all of them killed by the sea. The pressure wave from the explosion circled the Earth for five days, and for three years the sunsets of the world turned red.

But the most haunting thing about Krakatoa is not the destruction. It is the warning that came afterwards. In May 1883, with the volcano already erupting, eighty-six tourists from Batavia paid twenty-five guilders each to picnic on its crater. "Nobody thought of danger from that side," a Dutch engineer wrote. In 2012, four scientists modelled the collapse of the volcano that had grown in Krakatoa's place, Anak Krakatau, and calculated that its waves would reach the beach at Anyer in thirty-eight minutes. They wrote that a rapid detection and an alert system on the coast could make it harmless. On 22 December 2018, the volcano's flank collapsed almost exactly as they had described. There was no warning system for volcanic tsunamis, and at least 437 people died on the same shores.

In this documentary you will discover:
• why a volcano that had been silent for two centuries was treated as a tourist attraction
• how the last man to set foot on the island warned of "too much danger" fifteen days before the end
• what happened, minute by minute, on the morning of 27 August 1883
• how a single decision by a ship's captain saved every life aboard his steamer
• why the sound of the explosion may have been the loudest the Earth has ever made
• how the eruption changed the sunsets and the climate of the whole planet
• why a scientific paper predicted the next tsunami six years before it came

results.title: If Countries were hitted by Volcano of The Krakatoa #1883 #1883krakatoa #krakatoa
The Explosion That Reached Glasgow Seven Times
results.description:
Watch this wave cross your own city, with the original 1883 charts: https://science.coru.cc/en/this-explosion-crossed-your-city-seven-times/

One explosion. Seven passages over Glasgow, with the last more than five days later.

On 27 August 1883, Krakatoa erupted in the Sunda Strait. Its audible bang reached Perth and Rodrigues, roughly 3,110 and 4,800 km away. A much lower-frequency atmospheric pressure wave continued around the planet. Barographs recorded its first passages at Calcutta, Tokyo, Vienna and New York, then its return from the other direction. Glasgow's instrument recorded seven passages at about 11, 25, 48, 59, 84, 94 and 121 hours. These were pressure measurements, not seven audible explosions in Glasgow.

The globe fronts are idealized geometric illustrations paced to the story, not weather simulations or measured wave shapes. Station labels give the reported historical arrival hours; the Glasgow chart is a schematic showing their timing, not a copy of the original trace. The amber circles show distances to reported hearing locations, not a claim that everyone inside a circle heard the eruption. The 2022 Hunga Tonga sequence illustrates a separate eruption whose atmospheric pulse also circled Earth for days and whose audible booms were reported in Alaska, more than 9,000 km away. Hearing distance and loudness are different measurements.

Sources: Thomas B. Gabrielson, 'Krakatoa and the Royal Society' (Acoustics Today, 2010), drawing on the Royal Society report edited by G. J. Symons (1888); NOAA Science On a Sphere and CIMSS/SSEC on Hunga Tonga; Matoza et al., 'Atmospheric waves and global seismoacoustic observations of the January 2022 Hunga eruption, Tonga' (Science, 2022), via USGS; University of Alaska Fairbanks Geophysical Institute. Historical background and death toll: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa, Wikipedia, citing Symons and later studies. The official toll was 36,417, most killed by the tsunami.

Imagery: NASA Earth Observatory / Visible Earth, Blue Marble Next Generation (Reto Stöckli, NASA GSFC). Globe animation, circles, markers and schematic chart: Coru. Narration and rumble/explosion sound effects: ElevenLabs; the sounds are illustrative, not recordings of either eruption. Needle ticks synthesized locally. No music.

More Coru: use the website link in our channel profile.

results.description:
info erupsi gunung anak Krakatau hari ini.

gunung anak Krakatau kembali erupsi Dahsyat sejak kemarin hingga hari ini 10 Oktober 2026.

data sementara anak Krakatau sudah Meletus 14 kali hingga 10 Oktober 2026.

Status Gunung Anak Krakatau di Selat Sunda kembali naik dari Waspada (Level II) menjadi Siaga (Level III) sejak Jumat (9/10/2026) pukul 21.00 WIB. Masyarakat diimbau tidak beraktivitas dalam radius 5 kilometer dari pusat erupsi. Selain itu, aktivitas juga dilarang dalam radius 1 kilometer dari pulau baru di sektor barat laut dan tenggara Anak Krakatau.

 Badan Geologi Kementerian Energi dan Sumber Daya Mineral (ESDM) resmi menaikkan tingkat aktivitas Gunungapi Anak Krakatau di Selat Sunda dari Level II (Waspada) menjadi Level III (Siaga). Status baru tersebut berlaku terhitung sejak Jumat (9/10/2026) pukul 21.00 WIB.
Keputusan itu tertuang dalam surat bernomor 1729.Lap/GL.03/BGL/2026 tertanggal 9 Oktober 2026 yang ditandatangani Kepala Badan Geologi Lana Saria atas nama Menteri ESDM. Surat tersebut ditujukan kepada Kepala Badan Nasional Penanggulangan Bencana (BNPB), Gubernur Lampung, Gubernur Banten, Bupati Lampung Selatan, Bupati Serang, Bupati Pandeglang, serta Wali Kota Cilegon.


Berdasarkan hasil analisis dan evaluasi secara menyeluruh, maka tingkat aktivitas Gunungapi Anak Krakatau dinaikan dari Level II (Waspada) menjadi Level III (Siaga) terhitung mulai tanggal 9 Oktober 2026 pukul 21.00 WIB," tulis Badan Geologi dalam surat tersebut.

Badan Geologi mencatat, secara umum kegempaan vulkanik Anak Krakatau selama periode 21 September-9 Oktober 2026 belum menunjukkan peningkatan signifikan, dengan rata-rata kejadian di bawah lima kali per hari. Grafik RSAM (Real-time Seismic Amplitude Measurement) dan data tiltmeter juga belum memperlihatkan gejala peningkatan.

Meski demikian, lembaga tersebut menyebut peningkatan aktivitas dalam skala rendah mulai terlihat sejak awal Oktober 2026. Hal itu ditandai dengan 14 kali erupsi yang terjadi dalam rentang 6-9 Oktober 2026.

Pada 9 Oktober 2026 saja, hingga pukul 19.20 WIB, terjadi sembilan kali erupsi dengan amplitudo maksimum 55 mm dan durasi 32 detik. Tinggi kolom erupsi tidak teramati.
